elements.element: All licences granted to Customer extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 expressly extends all Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates.

elements.element: All licences granted to Customer extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 expressly extends all Section 2 licences to contractors acting on Corio's behalf.

elements.element: Every fully paid-up licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 is fully paid up and perpetual, but Section 2.3 is fully paid up without stating that its licence is perpetual.

elements.element: Every fully paid-up licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Neither fully paid-up licence in Sections 2.2 and 2.3 is stated to be irrevocable. Section 2.1 is irrevocable but is fee-bearing rather than fully paid up.

elements.element: Any subscription licence is terminable only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language does not identify or grant any subscription licence; therefore the condition triggering this requirement is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The licences remain nontransferable except under Section 14.1. That section permits certain assignments but requires consent for other assignments, including an M&A transaction involving the other party's direct competitor, and only benefits permitted successors and assigns.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered at least upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 provides broader automatic coverage to all Corio affiliates without requiring written notice, so affiliates are necessarily covered following any such notice.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 generally permits assignment in a merger, acquisition, or qualifying asset sale, but an M&A transaction involving a direct competitor of the other party still requires that party's consent. The fallback contains no such limitation.

result.reason: The added subsection clearly and effectively extends the licences to affiliates and contractors, but it does not cure the missing duration and irrevocability protections for all paid-up licences or provide an unrestricted M&A-successor transfer right. No complete playbook level is reached. The redline also adds a Corio compliance-responsibility condition not required by either position, although that condition is related and does not contradict the existing commercial terms.
